correctness.rationale: Generic hyperplane sections bijectively inherit j-faces from crossing (j+1)-faces of the cross-polytope. For any face with q below-threshold axes, 2^m-2^q-1[q=0] sign assignments straddle the plane, giving the full binomial f-vector. Comparing k=0,1 and strict decay of f0 for k>=1 gives exactly d-1 distinct face vectors. Invariant offsets yield ratios of expected half-normal consecutive spacings with the correct width normalization; integral probability sums equal one. Under normal-width size bias, max half-normal concentrates at sqrt(2log d), the number of above-offset axes has log exponent 1-U^2, and fixed-rank counts are asymptotic to 2^(j+1) l d^(j+1)/(j+1)!, proving joint exponent convergence. An extracted checker gives 945 exact finite combinatorial comparisons and quantitative quadrature/sampling tests; experiments do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A complete exact distribution of the entire f-vector under invariant affine slicing across all dimensions is a natural geometric probability invariant; the d-1 phase levels and exact positive integral weights are a full, nonarbitrary classification. The new joint logarithmic limit reveals perfect common random scaling across every fixed face rank, not obtainable from only a mean width, a central section, or one face count. It has explanatory value for high-dimensional polytope section complexity without relying on a downstream conjecture.
